description: ============================= linux-firmware ==========================

[Impact]

With kernel >= v7.3 or backport-iwlwifi-dkms >= 24.70, core API c107 and lower are supported, but it takes corresponding fw to take effect.

[Fix]

New 24.70 firmware are in:
* c5018ff6b11d ("iwlwifi: add Bz/Sc FW for core24.70-49 release")
* 181c33e757b0 ("iwlwifi: add Sc2/Wh FW for core24.70-99 release")

The former is available in linux-firmware/stonking starting from version 20260915.git1522c78a-0ubuntu1, but the latter is not yet tagged in either upstream or ubuntu linux-firmware. The latter is for Sc2 so moved into bug 2160682.

[Test Plan]

Check wifi link availability with `ip` or `iw`.

[Where problems could occur]

This adds the corresponding firmware blobs to existing platforms that are used to be driven by core 103 or lower API. The firmware blobs are opaque, stable fix come later if ever found.

[Other Info]

We are backporting core108 to Resolute in oem-7.3. Nominate for R, S and T. Yet the latter two already has it.

============================= backport-iwlwifi-dkms ========================

## FFE ##

[Rationale]

* Intel targets Nova Lake WiFi with 24.80 as planned in bug 2162157, yet the in-tree driver is not ready, and backport-iwlwifi 24.70 is the latest official release we may have so far. With backport-iwlwifi 24.70, we may drive the device with beta release firmwares. The final firmware is still pending for upstream review/verification.

[ Scope ]

* Support Intel WhP2 (BE211), SpP2 (BE213), LzP2 (AX221) WiFi/Bluetooth for Intel Nova Lake platforms.

* Add the output of seeded-in-ubuntu backport-iwlwifi-dkms.
  ```
  $ seeded-in-ubuntu backport-iwlwifi-dkms
  backport-iwlwifi-dkms's binaries are not seeded.
  ```

[ Regression Potential ]

* backport-iwlwifi-dkms is never recommended and is only used whenever the hardware enablement is given no other choice for cutting edge Intel WiFi generations. People are not supposed to use backport-iwlwifi-dkms whenever there are compatible alternatives, that is, kernels with same/newer UCODE/CORE firmware API levels. When used in hardware enablement in oem projects, it will be migrated to the in-tree iwlwifi driver whenever available. We don't switch from an in-tree iwlwifi driver to backport-iwlwifi-dkms.

* Migrating from 24.60 to 24.70, the backport compatibility is maintained as the lowest supported firmware level stays at core102.

* backport-iwlwifi-dkms contains more features than the in-tree iwlwifi driver of the same firmware level, but mostly are for features under experiment or for hardware generations in the future. Switching back to in-tree driver doesn't cause problems for the PV generation that a firmware level is meant for.

[ Testing ]

* Smoke test:
  - PPA: https://launchpad.net/~vicamo/+archive/ubuntu/sru-2159856-2
  - Build: https://launchpad.net/~vicamo/+archive/ubuntu/sru-2159856-2/+build/33621591/+files/buildlog_ubuntu-stonking-amd64.backport-iwlwifi-dkms_1%3A24.70-14867-0ubuntu1_BUILDING.txt.gz
  - Installation: <link to the installation test>
  - Upgrade: <link to the upgrade test>
  - Autopkgtest: <autopkgtest results>
  - Does it break other packages: N/A

https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/iwlwifi/backport-iwlwifi.git/log/?h=release/core24.70
Intel is switching to a release naming scheme used on Windows. by vicamo

2170922.last_activity_summary:
description: [ Impact ]

Backporting new firmware for HWE kernels to LTSes is a constant source of pain
and always results in problems. To limit the risk we always try to backport
only select firmwares that we think are safe but we never get it 100% correct.
The main issues are typically:

1. Some backported firmware that the HWE kernel needs is also loaded by the GA
   kernel which can cause issues for GA kernel users. New firmware with old
   kernels is a combination that firmware vendors typically don't test and is
   not really supported.

2. Missing HWE firmwares. Finding the exact firmwares that a particular kernel
   wants is not trivial. We're constantly missing blobs so when LTS users
   upgrade to a newer HWE kernel they sometimes experience regressions and HW
   that used to work no longer does because firmware is missing. We also
   deliberately exclude firmwares that we *think* might cause issues for GA
   kernel users.

3. Identifying and backporting firmwares is an expensive task and the results
   are never satisfying for both the firmware package maintainers and (more
   importantly) the users.

[ Fix ]

Introduce a new set of firmware packages: linux-firmware-hwe-<foo>. The idea
is that HWE kernels depend on linux-firmware-hwe (instead of linux-firmware)
which installs the same firmware binaries as the Ubuntu release where the HWE
kernel comes from. Take Resolute as an example. The first HWE kernel for
Resolute will be 7.3 from Stonking. The new set of linux-firmware-hwe for
Resolute will be a backport of linux-firmware from Stonking. The full set, no
backporting of individual blobs. That way we have the same combination of
kernel+firmware in both the interim and the LTS releases.

<foo> mirrors the linux-firmware subpackage split, e.g.
linux-firmware-hwe-amd-graphics vs linux-firmware-amd-graphics, with
linux-firmware-hwe as the umbrella metapackage pulling in the subpackage set.
There is only one HWE firmware set per release, not one per HWE kernel series.

Lifecycle per series:

* Interim releases: linux-firmware-hwe and every linux-firmware-hwe-<foo> are
  metapackages depending on their linux-firmware-<foo> counterparts. There is
  nothing to backport for interim releases (their GA kernel is the newest
  kernel) so the package names only exist to keep the namespace and dependency
  chain uniform across all series.

* LTS at release time: an LTS is the newest release when it comes out, so
  there is no HWE yet. The HWE kernel is just a metapackage depending on the
  GA kernel and linux-firmware-hwe follows suit and is also just a metapackage
  depending on linux-firmware.

* LTS once the first real HWE kernel lands: the HWE kernel metapackage is
  replaced by a real kernel package and linux-firmware-hwe-<foo> is replaced
  by real packages carrying the full firmware set from the HWE kernel's
  origin release. Real packages that provide firmware blobs only ever exist
  in LTS releases (Resolute and newer).

That way anything depending on linux-firmware-hwe-<foo> (e.g. HWE kernel
packages) resolves correctly on every series without per-series special
casing, and identical kernel+firmware combinations are guaranteed for both
the interim and the LTS releases.

The caveat with this is that it's not possible to have both linux-firmware
and linux-firmware-hwe installed at the same time (we might work around that
in the future). So you either have the firmwares for the GA kernel *or* the
firmwares for the HWE kernel. But you can have both GA *and* HWE kernels
installed at the same time. In that case and if you choose to boot the GA
kernel you'll run old kernel plus new firmware which could be problematic.
Because the real linux-firmware-hwe-<foo> packages replace metapackages that
previously pulled in the linux-firmware-<foo> counterparts, they will
Conflict/Replace (and possibly Provide) those to handle the upgrade cleanly.

[ Test Case ]

All verifications are package-level: package states via dpkg/apt, file lists
via dpkg -L, file contents via dpkg -V or debsums, and dependency resolution
via apt-get -s dry runs.

Note: no released LTS carries these packages yet, so the cases below need to
be run against test PPAs containing fake packages that mimic the real ones.

1. Dependency resolution
   kernel/firmware: GA/GA -> GA/HWE-shim

   Install the HWE kernel metapackage. Confirm that it Depends on
   linux-firmware-hwe and that linux-firmware-hwe resolves to
   linux-firmware. Complete the install and verify the expected package
   set is present.

   Steps:
     a. Start from a system with the GA kernel and linux-firmware
        installed and no HWE packages present.
     b. Dry-run: apt-get -s install <hwe-kernel-meta>
        Expected: resolves <hwe-kernel-meta> -> linux-firmware-hwe ->
        linux-firmware, with no linux-firmware removal.
     c. Install: apt-get install <hwe-kernel-meta>
     d. Verify: dpkg -l shows the HWE kernel metapackage,
        linux-firmware-hwe and linux-firmware-hwe-<foo> subpackages all
        installed, and linux-firmware still installed (not replaced).
     e. Verify: dpkg -L linux-firmware-hwe shows no files (pure
        metapackage) and the linux-firmware-hwe-<foo> packages have no
        file payload of their own.

2. File inventory parity
   kernel/firmware: GA/HWE-shim (unchanged)

   Verify that the installed linux-firmware-hwe set is content-identical
   to a stock linux-firmware install.

   Steps:
     a. Compare the dpkg -L file lists of every linux-firmware-hwe-<foo>
        package against its linux-firmware-<foo> counterpart. The lists
        must be identical.
     b. Verify file checksums of the installed files (dpkg -V or
        debsums). All files must pass.

3. Removal path
   kernel/firmware: GA/HWE-shim -> GA/GA

   Purge the HWE kernel metapackage and linux-firmware-hwe and verify
   that the GA firmware set is not taken down with it.

   Steps:
     a. apt-get purge <hwe-kernel-meta> linux-firmware-hwe
     b. Dry-run: apt-get -s autoremove
        Expected: linux-firmware and its subpackages are NOT candidates
        for removal.
     c. Verify: all firmware files from dpkg -L linux-firmware are still
        present on disk.

4. Freshly released LTS
   kernel/firmware: GA/GA -> GA/HWE-shim

   Repeat case 1 on a freshly released LTS, where linux-firmware-hwe is
   also just a metapackage.

   Steps:
     a. On a fresh LTS install: apt-get -s install <hwe-kernel-meta>
        shows the same resolution as in case 1.
     b. Install and verify the package set as in case 1.

5. Negative dependency test
   kernel/firmware: GA/GA (unchanged)

   Verify that GA kernel packages still depend on linux-firmware, not on
   linux-firmware-hwe.

   Steps:
     a. Inspect the GA kernel metapackage dependencies (dpkg -I or
        apt-cache show). The linux-firmware dependency must point at
        linux-firmware, not linux-firmware-hwe.
     b. Dry-run: apt-get -s install <ga-kernel-meta>
        Expected: the resolution does not include linux-firmware-hwe.

6. Opt-in install
   kernel/firmware: GA/GA -> HWE/HWE-real

   On an LTS with a real HWE kernel available, switching to the HWE
   kernel replaces linux-firmware with the real linux-firmware-hwe set.

   Steps:
     a. Start from a system with the GA kernel and linux-firmware
        installed. The HWE kernel and real linux-firmware-hwe packages
        are available from the test PPA.
     b. Dry-run: apt-get -s install <hwe-kernel-meta>
        Expected: linux-firmware is replaced by the real
        linux-firmware-hwe set, with no file conflicts reported.
     c. Install and verify the final state: the real linux-firmware-hwe
        set is installed, linux-firmware is gone, and dpkg --audit
        reports no half-configured packages.

7. Origin parity
   kernel/firmware: HWE/HWE-real (unchanged)

   Verify that the real linux-firmware-hwe set matches the firmware set
   of the HWE kernel's origin release exactly.

   Steps:
     a. In a chroot or container of the origin release, install its
        linux-firmware-<foo> packages and capture their file lists
        (dpkg -L) and checksums (/var/lib/dpkg/info/*.md5sums).
     b. Compare against the target's linux-firmware-hwe-<foo> packages:
        identical file lists and checksums, no missing and no extra
        blobs.

8. Co-install conflict
   kernel/firmware: HWE/HWE-real (unchanged, refused)

   Verify that linux-firmware and linux-firmware-hwe cannot be
   co-installed.

   Steps:
     a. With the real HWE set installed, dry-run: apt-get -s install
        linux-firmware. Expected: the resolver refuses due to the
        conflict.
     b. apt-get install linux-firmware linux-firmware-hwe: must fail
        cleanly, leaving dpkg --audit clean.

9. Kernel coexistence
   kernel/firmware: HWE/HWE-real (unchanged)

   Verify that the GA kernel package survives the firmware switch and
   record how its linux-firmware dependency is handled.

   Steps:
     a. After case 6: verify that the GA kernel package is still
        installed and intact (dpkg -l).
     b. Inspect how the GA kernel's dependency on linux-firmware is
        satisfied once linux-firmware is gone (e.g. via Provides from
        the HWE packages). Record the outcome; it must not leave any
        dpkg --audit findings.

10. Metapackage -> real, via -updates
    kernel/firmware: GA/HWE-shim -> HWE/HWE-real

    An LTS system with the metapackage-era linux-firmware-hwe installed
    receives the real HWE kernel and real firmware packages via
    -updates.

    Steps:
      a. Start from an LTS system in the GA/HWE-shim state.
      b. Enable the test PPA with the real HWE kernel and real firmware
         packages. Dry-run: apt-get -s dist-upgrade
         Expected: the linux-firmware-<foo> counterparts are removed,
         the real HWE set and real HWE kernel are installed, no
         conflicts reported.
      c. Apply the upgrade and verify: no dpkg errors, and no stale
         firmware files under /usr/lib/firmware belonging to the removed
         counterparts (compare dpkg -L output against the on-disk file
         inventory).

11. Real -> metapackage (reversal)
    kernel/firmware: HWE/HWE-real -> GA/GA

    Verify a clean revert from the real HWE arrangement back to the GA
    firmware set.

    Steps:
      a. Remove the real HWE kernel and the linux-firmware-hwe set.
      b. Install linux-firmware.
      c. Verify: complete file inventory restored (dpkg -L vs on-disk),
         checksums pass (dpkg -V), dpkg --audit clean.

Release upgrades -- one case per source -> target state transition of
linux-firmware-hwe. With no HWE packages installed, every path is a plain
linux-firmware release upgrade and serves as the shared baseline.

12. Shim -> shim
    kernel/firmware: (rel A) GA/HWE-shim -> (rel B) GA/HWE-shim

    E.g. interim -> interim. Metapackage arrangements on both sides, each
    resolving to its own release's linux-firmware.

    Steps:
      a. Start from a system in the GA/HWE-shim state on release A.
      b. do-release-upgrade to release B.
         Expected: the linux-firmware-hwe metapackages are present on
         both sides, the target release's linux-firmware is installed,
         no conflicts reported.
      c. Verify the final package set and file inventory on release B.

13. Shim -> real
    kernel/firmware: (interim) GA/HWE-shim -> (LTS) HWE/HWE-real

    Interim -> LTS after the target's HWE kernel has landed. The
    metapackage arrangement is replaced by the real packages and the
    real HWE kernel.

    Steps:
      a. Start from an interim system in the GA/HWE-shim state.
      b. do-release-upgrade to the LTS.
         Expected: the real linux-firmware-hwe set and real HWE kernel
         are installed, no conflicts reported.
      c. Verify the final package state as in case 6.

14. Real -> shim
    kernel/firmware: (LTS) HWE/HWE-real -> (interim/LTS) GA/HWE-shim

    LTS -> interim, and LTS -> LTS before the target's HWE kernel has
    landed. Run on both paths. The source carries real packages that
    Conflict with linux-firmware while the target is metapackage-era and
    wants linux-firmware.

    Steps:
      a. Start from an LTS system in the HWE/HWE-real state.
      b. do-release-upgrade to the target release.
         Expected: the real HWE set is removed, the target's
         linux-firmware is installed, and the upgrade completes without
         conflicts.
      c. Verify that no firmware files are lost (file inventory vs the
         target release's linux-firmware).

15. Real -> real
    kernel/firmware: (LTS A) HWE/HWE-real -> (LTS B) HWE/HWE-real

    LTS -> LTS after the target's HWE kernel has landed. The source's
    real set is replaced by the target's real set. This is a late-cycle
    case that only becomes testable once the target LTS has its own HWE
    kernel.

    Steps:
      a. Start from an LTS system in the HWE/HWE-real state on release A.
      b. do-release-upgrade to release B (which already has real HWE
         packages).
         Expected: the source's real set is replaced by release B's real
         set, no conflicts reported.
      c. Verify the final package state as in cases 6 and 7.

[ Where Problems Could Occur ]

* Incorrect or missing Conflicts/Replaces/Provides relationships between the
  real linux-firmware-hwe-<foo> packages and their linux-firmware-<foo>
  counterparts could cause file conflicts, failed upgrades, or a
  half-installed package state. Worst case, a system ends up with no firmware
  installed and fails to boot or loses hardware functionality after a
  reboot. Covered by test cases 6, 8, 10 and 14.

* If the backported firmware set is incomplete or the subpackage split
  doesn't match the origin release, firmware blobs required by the HWE kernel
  could be missing, causing hardware regressions on the HWE kernel
  (ironically the exact problem this design is meant to eliminate). Shipping
  the full, unmodified set from the origin release mitigates but does not
  fully eliminate this risk, e.g. if packaging bugs drop files. Covered by
  test case 7.

* Users who install the HWE firmware set but boot the GA kernel run old
  kernel + new firmware. This combination is not tested by firmware vendors
  and could cause regressions for GA kernel users, up to and including
  hardware that used to work no longer doing so.

* A firmware version skew between the linux-firmware-hwe-<foo> packages and
  the HWE kernel's expectations (e.g. if the origin release firmware gets
  updated without a corresponding re-backport) could lead to missing or
  incompatible firmware at HWE kernel runtime.

* Firmware may be required early (initramfs, root device, storage and
  graphics), so a botched transition between package states could leave a
  system unable to find firmware for its boot-critical devices after the
  next reboot. The lifecycle and release-upgrade transitions are covered
  explicitly by test cases 6, 10, 13 and 14.

* HWE kernel packages declare a hard Depends on linux-firmware-hwe, so kernel
  and firmware packages are upgraded together. However, firmware can be
  required at early boot (initramfs, root device, storage and graphics), so
  there is still a window during an upgrade where a new kernel is present
  but the matching firmware is not (or vice versa). Systems rebooting inside
  that window could see regressions until the upgrade completes. by juergh
